query: Can I see this on my phone? I'm working in ~/code/checkout on this laptop, and npm run dev is already serving the page at 127.0.0.1:3000. Both devices have Tailscale, but I haven't approved preview ports yet.
Share the running worktree on this MacBook privately with my review laptop. Tailscale is the App Store version. I approve unused HTTPS ports 8443-8445 here; please leave the app on 443 alone.
The app runs on our authorized dev host studio-dev at localhost:5173. Use its existing approved pool from the agent launch environment and send me a private mobile review link. No public deployment.

Keep the short hero, editorial hero and product-demo worktrees available at the same time. Publish three private links in home as one Landing review set, with titles that tell the designer what changed.

I explicitly need seven checkout variants numbered 1 through 7, not a pair. Startup for seven isolated instances is authorized and 8443-8452 is approved on this machine. Keep every version available for review.
There's no tailhome installation here and I don't want one. Give our designer a verified private Tailscale URL for the app already running on 127.0.0.1:8080. I approve 8443-8445 on this machine.

Check checkout-a, the preview you published yesterday. The card loads but I think /checkout is serving the generic landing screen. Verify that exact HTTPS route and tell me whether its home listing is current.
List the previews recorded by this skill under my account on the app machine. Show the Checkout layout set separately so I can choose what to remove; don't stop anything yet.

Remove checkout-a that you published on this machine, leaving checkout-b, the permanent 443 app and both dev processes running. A colleague may have edited one of checkout-a's Serve paths since yesterday.
We're done reviewing the exact set Checkout layout. Show a cleanup dry run, then remove its owned preview mappings on this machine. Leave Checkout layout mobile and the worktrees alone.

Our public payment provider must POST callbacks to localhost:3000/webhooks during testing. Use Tailscale Funnel to make that endpoint reachable without joining our tailnet; a private Serve link won't work.
Deploy the approved checkout branch to our production Vercel project and switch checkout.example.com to it. This replaces the customer-facing release, not a private worktree review.
The phone screenshot of localhost looks cramped. Update the React Preview component's responsive CSS and add Playwright coverage at 390px and 1280px. Do not publish or share a running app.
Tailpreview already owns the checkout preview and its Caddy lifecycle. Use Tailpreview's CLI to inspect its URL and shut it down after review; don't move it into direct Serve or add tailhome cards.
Our Portless app is already reachable privately. Diagnose its named localhost route using Portless's existing commands and keep Portless responsible for the listener and cleanup.
The studio-dev machine isn't on our tailnet yet. Install Tailscale, authenticate with a new auth key and enroll it before we discuss publishing any previews.
A teammate can't reach any of our private dev machines after yesterday's grants change. Audit the tailnet policy and propose the least-privilege access rule; don't create a new preview.
Set up tailhome from scratch on our server with OAuth, device filters and discovery ports. We already have preview URLs; this task is installing and configuring the launcher.
The home launcher has blank preview tiles after my CSS refactor. Fix the card grid rendering in the tailhome source and its UI tests; leave every published Serve mapping unchanged.

I have a manually managed private Serve service on 443, not one created by this skill. Review its reverse-proxy configuration and explain the 502 without adopting it, adding cards or changing its ownership.
